stem: Suresh has two children. Geeta is the daughter of Suresh. Hari is the brother of Geeta. Lakshmi is the mother of Geeta. Vinod is the son of Hari. How is Vinod related to Lakshmi?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Treating Vinod as being in the same generation as Hari (one below Lakshmi) rather than two generations below Lakshmi yields son instead of grandson.
Lakshmi is Geeta's mother, and Hari is Geeta's brother, so Hari is Lakshmi's son. Vinod is the son of Hari, so Vinod is Lakshmi's grandson.
Treating the relation from Lakshmi outward as through a sibling rather than a child gives nephew instead of grandson.
Misplacing Vinod three generations below Lakshmi yields grandnephew, an over-count of the generational distance.

explanation: Suresh and Lakshmi are parents (Lakshmi is mother of Geeta). Hari is Geeta's brother, so Hari is also Lakshmi's son. Vinod is Hari's son, therefore Vinod is Lakshmi's grandson.

explanation_sections.punchline: Hari is Lakshmi's son (sibling of Geeta, whose mother is Lakshmi); Vinod is Hari's son = Lakshmi's grandson.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply most-certain first: Lakshmi is mother of Geeta. Hari is brother of Geeta, so Hari is Lakshmi's son. Vinod is son of Hari. Chain: Lakshmi -> son Hari -> son Vinod. Vinod is Lakshmi's grandson.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always establish the common parent first, then count generation steps from there to the target.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 80 s. Trap: option 1 (son) by treating Hari as Lakshmi's husband rather than her son.
